text:
To: Regional Finance Controllers
From: Beatrix Lindqvist, Group Compliance
Subject: Revised delegation of authority

Following the external audit, the executive committee has approved a revised delegation of authority that takes effect on 1 July. Under the new framework, any commitment exceeding €50,000 must be countersigned by a second authorized [1], irrespective of the budget line to which it is charged. [2] Controllers who have until now approved such items unilaterally should therefore review every pending purchase order before the deadline.

The reforms are not intended to slow routine operations. [3], transactions below the threshold will continue to be processed under the existing workflow, provided that supporting documentation is attached. Should a controller fail to [4] with the procedure, the matter will be referred to the audit committee.

questions.explanation: The text requires a second authorized person to countersign: 'signatory' names that person, whereas 'signature', 'signal' and 'signage' are not people who can be authorized.

choices: The previous ceiling of €100,000 was introduced to speed up approvals, which had been reviewed only once since then.
The previous ceiling of €100,000 has been halved, which brings a far wider range of purchases under dual control.
Smaller purchases, by contrast, will remain under the single-signature rule that has applied for several years.
Several controllers had already begun to seek a second signature voluntarily, anticipating the revised framework.
questions.explanation: Only the first sentence explains why controllers who 'approved such items unilaterally' must now review orders ('therefore'): the ceiling was lowered. The others describe a past rule, smaller purchases, or voluntary behavior that contradicts 'until now approved ... unilaterally'.

The sentence contrasts the strict rule above with ordinary purchases that 'will continue' as before; 'conversely' marks that contrast, while 'accordingly', 'consequently' and 'thereafter' express result or sequence.
After 'fail to', the base verb is required, and 'comply with the procedure' is the fixed collocation; the other forms cannot follow 'to' here.

text:
Port Operators Brace for Tighter Emissions Rules

Operators of Europe's largest container terminals are preparing for regulations that will oblige vessels to switch off their engines while docked and draw power from the shore instead. The measure, which the transport commission describes as [1] to meeting its climate targets, is expected to cut emissions in port cities by almost a third.

[2] Few terminals possess the electrical capacity to supply several ships at once. Rotterdam's operator estimates that connecting its quays will cost more than €400 million, a sum it hopes to recover [3] higher berthing fees. Smaller ports, which cannot absorb such expenditure, have called for public subsidies. The commission has so far declined to commit itself, [4] it has acknowledged that unequal support could distort competition between harbors.

questions.explanation: The commission presents the measure as central to its climate targets; 'integral to' means essential, while 'incidental', 'peripheral' and 'ornamental' all suggest the opposite.

choices: Implementing the requirement was welcomed by shipping lines that had already invested heavily in cleaner engines.
Implementing the requirement will nevertheless prove considerably more demanding in practice than the announcement suggests.
The requirement applies to passenger ferries as well as freight vessels, which dock in the same quays.
Compliance with the requirement will be checked by inspectors during routine visits to each of the quays.
questions.explanation: The next sentence ('Few terminals possess the electrical capacity') supports a difficulty; only the first option announces that implementation will be demanding. The others describe welcome, scope or inspection and do not lead to the capacity problem.
'Recover a sum through higher berthing fees' states the means; 'despite', 'notwithstanding' and 'regardless' introduce a contrast, which makes no sense here.
The commission has declined to commit, 'although' it acknowledges the risk of distortion: a concession. 'Because' and 'unless' do not fit the logic, and 'whereas' would contrast two unrelated facts.

text:
Dear Professor Aldana,

On behalf of the Hartwell Trust, I am pleased to confirm that your application for funding has been approved in principle. The award, totaling £180,000 over three years, is [1] upon the satisfactory completion of an ethical review, which our panel will arrange once your team has submitted the revised protocol.

[2] Disbursement will occur in annual installments, the first of which will be released within thirty days of the review's outcome. The Trust expects to be kept informed of any significant deviation from the agreed timetable. [3] a delay prove unavoidable, you are asked to notify the program officer in writing at the earliest opportunity, [4] the matter can be considered before the next installment falls due.

Yours sincerely,
Marguerite Ellison
Director of Grants

questions.explanation: 'Contingent upon' is the fixed collocation meaning dependent on a condition ('is contingent upon the satisfactory completion'); 'conditioned', 'reliant' and 'bound' do not take 'upon' in this sense.

choices: Please note that the review will be conducted by the same panel that assessed your original application last spring.
Please note that this approval does not constitute a binding commitment until the formal agreement has been countersigned.
Please note that installments have been calculated on the basis of the revised budget you submitted earlier.
Please note that the Trust has funded comparable projects in other universities during the past decade.
questions.explanation: The next sentence begins 'Disbursement will occur', continuing the terms of the award; only the first sentence qualifies the approval as non-binding, setting up the conditions that follow. The others add unrelated detail about the panel, the budget or past projects.

'Should a delay prove unavoidable' is the inverted conditional, equivalent to 'If a delay proves unavoidable'; 'whereas', 'unless' and 'albeit' cannot introduce an inverted clause with the subjunctive 'prove'.
'so that the matter can be considered' states the purpose; 'in order' lacks 'that' or 'to', 'such that' expresses result, and 'lest' requires a negative idea.

text:
To: All Department Heads
From: Kwame Asante, Chief Operating Officer
Subject: Interim hiring restrictions

In view of the revenue shortfall reported at the end of the second quarter, the board has asked that all non-essential recruitment be suspended with immediate effect. [1] Vacancies that have already been advertised will be [2] only where the post is directly linked to a contractual obligation to a client.

I appreciate that this decision will place additional pressure on teams that are already stretched. [3], I would ask you to resist the temptation to redistribute workloads informally; any adjustment should be agreed with Human Resources beforehand so that overtime is [4] correctly. The restrictions will be reviewed at the end of the financial year.

choices: Positions that arise through resignation will not be refilled automatically, and each one will be assessed individually.
Positions that were created last spring will be filled automatically, and each one will be assessed individually.
Employees who resign will be asked to work their notice period, and each case will be assessed individually.
Positions that arise through resignation had been refilled automatically, and each one was assessed individually.
questions.explanation: The next sentence begins 'Vacancies that have already been advertised', so the preceding sentence must concern vacancies arising now; the first option does, whereas the others contradict the freeze, shift the subject to notice periods, or use a past tense that does not match the announcement.
The passive 'will be pursued' needs the past participle; the other forms are grammatically impossible after 'be'.

The writer acknowledges the pressure, 'nevertheless' introducing the request to resist informal redistribution; 'furthermore' and 'likewise' add, and 'therefore' would wrongly present the request as a result of the pressure.
'Overtime is recorded correctly' is a passive with a past participle; the other forms do not fit after 'is'.

text:
Book Review: The Quiet Ledger

In her study of mid-century accounting practices, historian Odile Marchetti argues that the profession's reputation for neutrality was less a fact than a carefully cultivated image. Drawing on previously unexamined firm archives, she shows how auditors routinely [1] findings in order to preserve long-standing client relationships.

[2] The evidence, however, is not always presented with equal rigor. Several chapters rest on a single set of internal memoranda, [3] others rely on interviews conducted decades after the events described. Readers seeking a definitive account will be disappointed. Those who wish to understand how professional ethics evolve under commercial pressure, [4], will find the book both lucid and provocative.

questions.explanation: Auditors who wished to preserve client relationships would 'soften' their findings, making them less severe; the other verbs would not protect relationships.

choices: This central claim has been challenged repeatedly, and it is rejected by most contemporary scholars of the period.
This central claim is argued persuasively, and it is supported by a wealth of detail drawn from private correspondence.
This earlier claim was argued persuasively, and it was supported by detail drawn from private correspondence.
This central claim is argued persuasively, yet it is supported by no detail drawn from private correspondence.
questions.explanation: The next sentence begins 'The evidence, however, is not always presented with equal rigor', which contrasts with a positive judgment; only the first option offers that praise. The others reject the claim, change its time reference, or deny any evidence, which would make 'however' illogical.
The sentence contrasts one chapter type with another ('Several chapters ... whereas others'); 'therefore', 'moreover' and 'hence' do not express contrast.
'By contrast' is the only option that sets those seeking a definitive account against those who want to understand ethics; the others do not mark opposition.

text:
NOTICE TO LEASEHOLDERS
Dunmore Court Residents' Company

Following a structural survey commissioned last quarter, the freeholder has confirmed that the east elevation requires substantial remedial work. [1] Scaffolding will be erected from 3 March, and access to the affected balconies will be restricted for approximately five months.

The cost of the work will be apportioned among leaseholders in proportion to the size of each apartment. [2] a leaseholder is unable to settle the charge in a single payment, an installment arrangement may be requested through the managing agent. [3] any dispute over the apportionment, leaseholders may submit a written objection by 20 February. The surveyor will [4] the findings at an open meeting on 12 February.

choices: Delaying the repairs would, in the surveyor's judgment, expose both residents and passers-by to an unacceptable risk of falling masonry.
Delaying the repairs would, in the surveyor's judgment, have reduced the cost for residents and the freeholder alike.
Postponing the repairs would, in the freeholder's view, lower the insurance premium for residents and passers-by.
Beginning the repairs would, in the surveyor's judgment, expose both residents and passers-by to unacceptable noise levels.
questions.explanation: The next sentence reports scaffolding and restricted access, a consequence of urgency; only the first option gives a safety reason why the work cannot wait. The others claim savings, a lower premium, or present the repairs themselves as the hazard.
'In the event that a leaseholder is unable to settle' introduces a possible, hypothetical situation; 'inasmuch as' would state it as fact, and 'notwithstanding that' and 'albeit' express concession.
'In the event of any dispute' is the fixed expression for a possible occurrence; 'in lieu of' means instead of, 'in pursuit of' means seeking, and 'in excess of' means above.
A surveyor 'presents' findings at a meeting; 'prescribe' means order, 'preside' takes 'over', and 'preclude' means prevent.

text:
Regulator Fines Retailer Over Customer Data Lapse

Europe's data protection authority has fined the retailer Kessmann €4.2 million after an investigation found that the personal details of some 600,000 customers had been stored without adequate [1]. The company, which maintains that it acted lawfully, has announced that it will appeal.

[2] That distinction proved decisive. [3] Kessmann had encrypted the data held on its main servers, it failed to apply the same standard to backup copies, which were left accessible to employees who had no need to consult them. Investigators noted that no evidence had emerged that the information had been misused. They concluded, however, that the exposure alone [4] a breach of the regulation.

questions.explanation: Data stored 'without adequate safeguards' is the fixed collocation; 'safeties', 'sureties' (financial guarantees) and 'shelters' do not refer to protective measures for data.

choices: The authority drew a line between customers who had consented to marketing and those who had declined it.
The authority drew a line between data held on the company's main servers and copies retained for backup purposes.
The authority drew a line between staff who were authorized to view records and those who were excluded from them.
The authority drew a line between retailers that operate online and those that continue to trade only in stores.
questions.explanation: 'That distinction' must refer back to a distinction that the next sentences develop: encrypted main servers versus unprotected backups. Only the first option sets this up; the others describe distinctions that the following text never uses.
'Although' introduces a clause ('Kessmann had encrypted the data'); 'notwithstanding', 'despite' and 'regardless of' must be followed by a noun phrase, not a full clause.
'Constituted a breach' means amounted to a breach; 'comprised' means included, 'consisted' requires 'of', and 'contributed' requires 'to'.

text:
To: Procurement Team
From: Dagmar Reinholt, Head of Sourcing
Subject: Supplier tender – shortlisting criteria

The tender for packaging materials closed on Friday, and fourteen bids were received. Before we begin the evaluation, I should like to clarify how the shortlist will be drawn up, since several of you have asked whether price will be the deciding factor.

It will not. [1] Bids will be scored on quality, delivery reliability and environmental performance, with cost accounting for no more than 30 percent of the total. [2] a bidder's price is markedly lower than the others, we shall request a written justification, as unrealistically low offers have in the past [3] contractual disputes. Each evaluator should score the bids independently and submit the results to me by Thursday, [4] the panel can meet on Friday to reconcile any discrepancies.

choices: Experience has shown that the cheapest offer rarely proves the most economical once defects and late deliveries are taken into account.
Experience has shown that the cheapest offer rarely proves the most reliable once prices and discounts are taken into account.
Experience has shown that the most expensive offer rarely proves the most economical once defects and delays are ignored.
Experience has shown that the cheapest supplier rarely proves the most economical until defects and delays are taken into account.
questions.explanation: The next sentence says bids will be scored on quality, reliability and environment with cost limited to 30 percent; only the first option explains why price should not dominate. The others confuse price with reliability, ignore defects, or suggest that the most expensive offer is the problem.

'Where a bidder's price is markedly lower' introduces a specific situation in which the rule applies; 'whereas' would contrast two facts, 'whether' needs an alternative, and 'wherever' would claim it holds in every place.
Low offers have 'precipitated' (triggered) disputes; 'predicated' means based, 'prescribed' means ordered, and 'predisposed' means inclined.
'so that the panel can meet' states the purpose of the deadline; 'in order' needs 'to' or 'that', 'provided' needs 'that', and 'lest' requires a negative result.
